Natural_Language: This part implements simplified procedures for the acquisition of noncommercial products and services valued at or below the simplified acquisition threshold (SAT) in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901-1903, 1905, and 3305.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_000_a: This part implements simplified procedures for acquisition of noncommercial products and services; P_13_000_b: Acquisitions are valued at or below the SAT; P_13_000_c: Procedures are in accordance with 41 U.S.C. 1901-1903, 1905, and 3305
Validation_Notes: Declarative scope statement establishing Part 13 coverage. Three conjuncts define what (simplified procedures for noncommercial), threshold (at or below SAT), and statutory authority. Straightforward conjunction.

Natural_Language: Applicability requirements for use of simplified procedures for noncommercial acquisitions under this part.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001: Applicability consists of conditions for use, procedural requirements with exceptions, prohibition on splitting, and reference to inapplicable laws
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for section 13.001. All four subsections collectively define when and how Part 13 procedures apply.

Natural_Language: The procedures in this part may be used only if there are no commercial products or commercial services that can satisfy the agency's needs (see part 12) and the supplies or services are not available from a required source (see part 8).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_a_1: No commercial products or commercial services can satisfy agency's needs; P_13_001_a_2: Supplies or services are not available from a required source
Validation_Notes: Both conditions must be met before Part 13 procedures may be used. The 'only if' language creates a biconditional gate, but because this is a permissive 'may be used' rather than mandatory, conjunction of prerequisites is the accurate formalization. Commercial availability (Part 12) and required source (Part 8) must both be ruled out.

Natural_Language: There are no commercial products or commercial services that can satisfy the agency's needs (see part 12).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_a_1: No commercial products or commercial services can satisfy agency's needs
Validation_Notes: Negation of commercial product/service availability. This is a factual determination the agency must make before using Part 13. References Part 12 for commercial item procedures.

Natural_Language: The supplies or services are not available from a required source (see part 8).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_a_2: Supplies or services are not available from a required source
Validation_Notes: Negation of required source availability. Agency must verify no required source (e.g., AbilityOne, Federal Prison Industries) can fill the need before using Part 13. References Part 8.

Natural_Language: Follow the procedures in this part when procuring noncommercial products and services valued at greater than the micro-purchase threshold (MPT) but at or below the SAT, except when procuring architect-engineering services, construction as a noncommercial service, or research and development.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_b_1: Procurement is for noncommercial products and services; P_13_001_b_2: Value is greater than MPT but at or below SAT; P_13_001_b_3: Procurement is not for architect-engineering services; P_13_001_b_4: Procurement is not for construction as noncommercial service; P_13_001_b_5: Procurement is not for research and development
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition with conditional structure. When all five conditions are met (noncommercial, within threshold range, and none of the three exceptions apply), Part 13 procedures are mandatory ('follow'). HIGH-RISK due to material implication. The exceptions are carved out as negations in the antecedent rather than separate conditionals.

Natural_Language: When procuring architect-engineering services, follow the short selection process at 36.602-5.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_b_1_a: Procurement is for architect-engineering services; P_13_001_b_1_b: Follow short selection process at 36.602-5
Validation_Notes: Conditional exception: when the procurement is for A-E services, the mandatory action is to follow 36.602-5 instead of Part 13. HIGH-RISK due to material implication but the conditional trigger is unambiguous.

Natural_Language: When procuring construction as a noncommercial service, comply with the requirements in part 36 for construction contracts and subpart 22.4 on labor standards for contracts involving construction.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_b_2_a: Procurement is for construction as noncommercial service; P_13_001_b_2_b: Comply with Part 36 requirements for construction contracts; P_13_001_b_2_c: Comply with subpart 22.4 on labor standards for contracts involving construction
Validation_Notes: Conditional exception with conjunctive consequent. When construction is procured as noncommercial, both Part 36 and Subpart 22.4 compliance are mandatory. Two separate regulatory regimes apply simultaneously.

Natural_Language: When procuring research and development, use the procedures in this part in conjunction with the procedures in part 35, as appropriate.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_b_3_a: Procurement is for research and development; P_13_001_b_3_b: Use Part 13 procedures in conjunction with Part 35 procedures
Validation_Notes: Conditional exception for R&D. Unlike the other two exceptions which replace Part 13, this one supplements Part 13 with Part 35. 'As appropriate' introduces discretion but the core requirement (use both) is mandatory. HIGH-RISK due to implication.

Natural_Language: Do not divide requirements, the aggregate value of which exceeds the SAT, merely to permit use of the procedures in this part.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_c_a: Requirements have aggregate value exceeding SAT; P_13_001_c_b: Requirements are divided merely to permit use of Part 13 procedures
Justification_Rules: Negation (Neg): Rule 10; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; De Morgan's Rule (DeM): Rule 11
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on requirement splitting. The negation applies to the conjunction of both conditions: having aggregate value above SAT AND dividing solely to use Part 13. This is the anti-bundling/splitting rule. Splitting for legitimate reasons (different delivery schedules, different vendors) is not prohibited.

Natural_Language: Go to https://www.acquisition.gov/inapplicablelaws for the lists of laws that do not apply to acquisitions valued at or below the SAT (41 U.S.C. 1905).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_001_d: Reference to list of inapplicable laws for acquisitions at or below SAT per 41 U.S.C. 1905
Validation_Notes: Informational reference directing users to external resource. No logical operation required beyond identity. The statutory citation (41 U.S.C. 1905) provides the legal basis for law exemptions below SAT.

Natural_Language: Competition requirements for noncommercial acquisitions at or below the SAT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_101: Competition requirements consist of mandatory competition promotion and permissive single-source authority
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for competition section. Both the mandatory competition promotion and the permissive single-source exception together define the competition framework.

Natural_Language: Agencies must promote competition to the maximum extent practicable when procuring noncommercial products and services valued at or below the SAT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_101_a_1: Agency is procuring noncommercial products and services at or below SAT; P_13_101_a_2: Agency promotes competition to maximum extent practicable
Validation_Notes: Mandatory requirement triggered by procurement activity within scope. 'Must' is mandatory. 'Maximum extent practicable' introduces a qualified standard but does not create discretion -- the obligation to promote competition is absolute, only the degree is bounded by practicability. HIGH-RISK due to implication.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers may solicit from a single source based on a determination and findings (see subpart 1.5) that only one source is reasonably available (e.g., urgency, exclusive licensing agreements, brand-name or industrial mobilization).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_101_b_a: Contracting officer makes determination and findings per subpart 1.5; P_13_101_b_b: Only one source is reasonably available; P_13_101_b_c: Contracting officer solicits from single source
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority ('may') with two prerequisites: D&F per subpart 1.5 AND only one source reasonably available. Tautology in consequent represents CO discretion. Examples (urgency, exclusive licensing, brand-name, industrial mobilization) are illustrative, not exhaustive. Both conditions are necessary but not sufficient for single-source solicitation.

Natural_Language: Acquisitions of supplies or services that have an anticipated dollar value above the MPT, but at or below the SAT, must be set aside for small business concerns (see part 19).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_102_a: Acquisition has anticipated dollar value above MPT but at or below SAT; P_13_102_b: Acquisition is set aside for small business concerns
Validation_Notes: Mandatory set-aside requirement. 'Must' creates binding obligation. When value falls in the MPT-to-SAT range, small business set-aside is not discretionary. References Part 19 for implementation details. HIGH-RISK due to implication but the conditional trigger (dollar value range) and consequence (set-aside) are both unambiguous.

Natural_Language: Generally, inspection and acceptance should be at destination. Inspection at the supplier's location should be specified only if required by 46.404.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_103_a: Inspection and acceptance is at destination; P_13_103_b: Inspection at supplier's location is specified; P_13_103_c: Inspection at supplier's location is required by 46.404
Validation_Notes: Advisory 'should' for destination inspection (non-binding default). Second sentence creates a conditional: supplier-location inspection is permitted only when 46.404 requires it, effectively a biconditional on that specific requirement. 'Generally' and 'should' reduce enforceability. PENDING_REVIEW due to advisory language and HIGH-RISK implication.

Natural_Language: Follow the simplified procedures at 12.201-1 for issuing requests for quotations (RFQs). Agencies are encouraged to use additional innovative approaches and may leverage the other flexibilities identified in that section; however, if using blanket purchase agreements (BPAs), the maximum value of each individual purchase under a BPA may not exceed the SAT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_201_a: Follow simplified procedures at 12.201-1 for issuing RFQs; P_13_201_b: Agencies are encouraged to use additional innovative approaches; P_13_201_c: Agencies may leverage other flexibilities in 12.201-1; P_13_201_d: BPAs are used; P_13_201_e: Maximum value of each individual purchase under BPA does not exceed SAT
Justification_Rules: Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]
Validation_Notes: Complex multi-part provision. First clause is mandatory ('follow'). Second is advisory ('encouraged'). Third is permissive ('may') represented as tautology. Fourth is a conditional restriction on BPAs. The BPA cap is mandatory ('may not exceed') despite the surrounding permissive language.

Natural_Language: Follow the procedures in 12.203 when establishing evaluation factors and a process to evaluate quotations in an efficient and minimally burdensome manner. Notify potential quoters of the basis on which the agency will make the award decision. Exercise good business judgment in deciding whether or not to accept a quotation received after the due date or time.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_202_a: Follow procedures in 12.203 for establishing evaluation factors and evaluation process; P_13_202_b: Evaluation is efficient and minimally burdensome; P_13_202_c: Notify potential quoters of basis for award decision; P_13_202_d: Exercise good business judgment on late quotations
Validation_Notes: Four mandatory requirements stated as imperative commands ('follow,' 'notify,' 'exercise'). All four apply simultaneously. Good business judgment on late quotations creates bounded discretion but the obligation to exercise judgment is itself mandatory.

Natural_Language: Award procedures for simplified noncommercial acquisitions including price reasonableness, documentation, and forms.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_203: Award procedures consist of price reasonableness, documentation, and forms requirements
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for award section. All three subsections are independent requirements that apply to every award.

Natural_Language: The contracting officer must determine the price to be fair and reasonable. Whenever possible, base price reasonableness on competitive quotations.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_203_a_1: Contracting officer determines price to be fair and reasonable; P_13_203_a_2: Price reasonableness is based on competitive quotations when possible
Validation_Notes: First sentence is mandatory ('must'). Second sentence is advisory ('whenever possible') but still an obligation to attempt competitive basis. Both requirements apply to every award action.

Natural_Language: Include in the contract file a written description of the procedures used in awarding the purchase order and the number of quotations received.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_203_b_1: Contract file includes written description of procedures used in awarding purchase order; P_13_203_b_2: Contract file includes number of quotations received
Validation_Notes: Mandatory documentation requirement. Both elements (procedure description and quotation count) must be in the contract file. Imperative 'include' is treated as mandatory.

Natural_Language: Use the Optional Form (OF) 347, Order for Supplies or Services; the OF 336, Continuation Sheet, or OF 348, Order for Supplies and Services Schedule-Continuation; or similar agency forms or automated formats to the maximum extent practicable.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_203_c_a: Use OF 347; P_13_203_c_b: Use OF 336 or OF 348; P_13_203_c_c: Use similar agency forms or automated formats; P_13_203_c_d: Usage is to maximum extent practicable
Validation_Notes: Disjunctive choice among form options (OF 347, OF 336/348, or similar forms) conjoined with the qualifier 'to maximum extent practicable.' Any of the form options satisfies the requirement, but the obligation to use standard forms is qualified, not absolute.

Natural_Language: Contract clauses requirements for noncommercial acquisitions at or below the SAT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_204: Contract clause requirements consist of prescribed clause inclusion, permissive use of 52.213-4, and prohibition on Part 12 clauses
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for contract clauses section. All three subsections define the clause framework for noncommercial simplified acquisitions.

Natural_Language: Include clauses prescribed elsewhere in the FAR in purchase orders for noncommercial supplies or services valued at or below the SAT as required or applicable based on the clause prescriptions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_204_a_1: Clauses prescribed elsewhere in FAR are included in purchase orders; P_13_204_a_2: Purchase orders are for noncommercial supplies or services at or below SAT; P_13_204_a_3: Inclusion is based on clause prescriptions (as required or applicable)
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement. When purchase orders are for noncommercial at or below SAT, prescribed clauses must be included per their individual prescriptions. The 'as required or applicable' qualifier means each clause's own prescription determines whether it applies. HIGH-RISK due to implication.

Natural_Language: Contracting officers may use the clause at 52.213-4, Terms and Conditions-Simplified Acquisitions (Noncommercial), to provide a streamlined set of terms and conditions for inspection/acceptance, excusable delays, terminations, and warranties. This clause is either used in lieu of similar clauses prescribed for these purposes or tailored to incorporate only some of the streamlined terms and conditions, as necessary.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_204_b_a: CO uses clause 52.213-4; P_13_204_b_b: Clause provides streamlined terms for inspection/acceptance, excusable delays, terminations, and warranties; P_13_204_b_c: Clause is used in lieu of similar prescribed clauses; P_13_204_b_d: Clause is tailored to incorporate only some streamlined terms
Justification_Rules: Tautology (Taut): Rule 18; Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Disjunction (Disj): Rule 8
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority ('may') to use 52.213-4 represented as tautology. If used, the clause serves its stated purpose (streamlined terms) AND must be deployed in one of two ways: full replacement of similar clauses OR tailored partial incorporation. The choice between full use and tailoring is disjunctive.

Natural_Language: Do not use part 12 clauses (i.e., 52.212-1, 52.212-2, or 52.212-4) in noncommercial acquisitions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_204_c_a: Acquisition is noncommercial; P_13_204_c_b: Part 12 clauses (52.212-1, 52.212-2, 52.212-4) are used
Validation_Notes: Prohibition on using commercial clauses in noncommercial acquisitions. 'Do not use' is a mandatory prohibition. The 'i.e.' indicates the list (52.212-1, -2, -4) is exhaustive, not illustrative. This creates a bright-line rule with no exceptions.

Natural_Language: Comply with the award notice posting requirements in subpart 5.3. Upon request, provide a brief explanation of the award decision that explains why the unsuccessful quoter was not selected. If an award notice was not required to be posted to the Government point of entry, also provide the information that would be included in an award notice (see 5.301(c)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_301_a: Comply with award notice posting requirements in subpart 5.3; P_13_301_b: Upon request, provide brief explanation of award decision to unsuccessful quoter; P_13_301_c: Award notice was not required to be posted to Government point of entry; P_13_301_d: Provide information that would be included in award notice per 5.301(c)
Validation_Notes: Three requirements: (1) mandatory posting compliance, (2) mandatory explanation upon request, and (3) conditional additional information when no public posting was required. The third element uses material implication -- when no GPE posting occurred, additional information must be provided directly.

Natural_Language: Cancellations and terminations procedures for purchase orders.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_302: Cancellation and termination procedures consist of government withdrawal rights, written acceptance requests, and procedures for contested cancellations
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for cancellations and terminations section. All three subsections address sequential steps in the cancellation/termination process.

Natural_Language: The Government may withdraw, amend, or cancel purchase orders by written notice to the supplier at any time before acceptance of the order occurs (see 12.201-1(b)).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_302_a_1: Acceptance of purchase order has not occurred; P_13_302_a_2: Government provides written notice to supplier; P_13_302_a_3: Government withdraws, amends, or cancels purchase order
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Tautology (Taut): Rule 18
Validation_Notes: Permissive authority ('may') with two prerequisites: before acceptance AND with written notice. Tautology represents government discretion to act or not. The three actions (withdraw, amend, cancel) are disjunctive options within the tautological consequent. Time constraint (before acceptance) is the critical gate.

Natural_Language: If the supplier did not accept the purchase order in writing, request that the supplier provide written acceptance of the cancellation.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_302_b_a: Supplier did not accept purchase order in writing; P_13_302_b_b: Request supplier to provide written acceptance of cancellation
Validation_Notes: Conditional obligation. When supplier has not provided written acceptance of the original PO, the CO must request written acceptance of cancellation. This creates a documentation trail for unaccepted orders. 'Request' is imperative, making it mandatory.

Natural_Language: If the contractor does not accept the cancellation or claims that costs were incurred as a result of the contractor beginning performance under the purchase order, follow the procedures in part 49 or 52.213-4 to terminate the purchase order.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_302_c_a: Contractor does not accept cancellation; P_13_302_c_b: Contractor claims costs were incurred from beginning performance; P_13_302_c_c: Follow procedures in Part 49 to terminate; P_13_302_c_d: Follow procedures in 52.213-4 to terminate
Validation_Notes: Conditional with disjunctive antecedent and disjunctive consequent. Either contractor refusal OR cost claims triggers mandatory termination procedures. CO has choice between Part 49 or clause 52.213-4 for the termination method. Both triggers are independent -- either alone is sufficient.

Natural_Language: Contract financing and payments for simplified noncommercial acquisitions.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_303: Financing and payment requirements consist of financing prohibition and payment procedure reference
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for financing and payments section. Both subsections apply to all simplified noncommercial acquisitions.

Natural_Language: Unless agency regulations permit otherwise, do not provide financing for purchases valued at or below the SAT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_303_a_1: Agency regulations permit financing; P_13_303_a_2: Purchases are valued at or below SAT; P_13_303_a_3: Financing is provided for purchases
Justification_Rules: Material Implication (Impl): Rule 15 [HIGH-RISK]; Conjunction (Conj): Rule 7; Negation (Neg): Rule 10
Validation_Notes: Prohibition with exception. Default rule: no financing at or below SAT. Exception: agency regulations can override. Formalized as: when purchases are at/below SAT AND agency regs do NOT permit, then financing is prohibited. The 'unless' clause creates the carve-out in the antecedent.

Natural_Language: See part 32 for payment procedures, including the option to use fast payment procedures.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_303_b: Payment procedures are per Part 32, including option for fast payment
Validation_Notes: Reference provision directing to Part 32 for payment procedures. 'Option to use fast payment' notes an available but non-mandatory procedure within Part 32.

Natural_Language: Micro-purchase procedures and automatic clause application.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_401: Micro-purchase requirements consist of procedural reference and automatic clause application
Validation_Notes: Parent proposition for micro-purchases section. Both subsections apply to all micro-purchase transactions.

Natural_Language: Follow the procedure in 12.4 when making purchases valued at or below the MPT.
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_401_a_1: Purchase is valued at or below MPT; P_13_401_a_2: Follow procedure in 12.4
Validation_Notes: Conditional requirement. When purchase value is at or below MPT, section 12.4 procedures are mandatory ('follow'). This bridges Part 13 to Part 12's micro-purchase provisions. HIGH-RISK due to implication.

Natural_Language: While micro-purchases do not require written provision or clauses, the clause at 52.232-39, Unenforceability of Unauthorized Obligations, automatically applies to any micro-purchase, including those made with the Governmentwide commercial purchase card. This clause prevents violations of the Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. 1341).
Atomic_Propositions: P_13_401_b_a: Micro-purchases do not require written provisions or clauses; P_13_401_b_b: Clause 52.232-39 automatically applies to any micro-purchase; P_13_401_b_c: Automatic application includes purchases made with Governmentwide commercial purchase card; P_13_401_b_d: Clause 52.232-39 prevents violations of Anti-Deficiency Act (31 U.S.C. 1341)
Validation_Notes: Four conjunctive statements. First establishes general rule (no written clauses needed). Second creates exception (52.232-39 applies automatically regardless). Third clarifies scope includes purchase card transactions. Fourth states purpose (Anti-Deficiency Act compliance). No discretion -- all four are declarative facts about how the regulation operates.
